risks.text: Committed cost against a spot revenue book: ~$279bn of not-yet-commenced leases and 5.5-year asset lives behind revenue with no take-or-pay. FY2022 precedent: revenue -1%, operating income -38%, on a cost base one third the size of 2027's
The compute has no second buyer: open-weighting Muse Spark 1.2 and Muse Glimmer forfeits any licensing annuity, so $137bn a year must be recovered from advertising alone
No one can stop it: 61% of votes in one hand, capex guidance raised twice in 2026, buyback suspended, dividend debt-funded, equity offering reportedly considered
Duration risk: ~87% of DCF value is terminal, so each 100bp of discount rate removes ~17% of equity value, with the 10-year already at its highest since November 2023
Competitive: OpenAI ad run-rate went from ~$100m to ~$1bn in six months and TikTok's US joint venture is newly unencumbered with US advertisers

conclusions: Triangulated probability-weighted fair value is $496 against a price of $615.20 - a 19.3% overvaluation - weighting SOTP 30%, DCF 35%, EV/IC 25% and P/B-ROE 10% across a 30/45/25 scenario set.

Expected three-year IRR is 4.5% against a 10.0% cost of equity and a 4.79% risk-free rate. That, rather than the fair-value gap, is the decisive number: mega-cap equity risk for approximately a Treasury return.

The headline 35% peer discount is about 32 points explained by zero free cash flow, a zero-contract revenue book, controlled-company governance and litigation. The unexplained residual is roughly 3 points of P/E, about 11% - not enough on its own to buy the stock.

About 87% of DCF value is terminal in every scenario, which is why the DCF is weighted at 35% and the SOTP - the only method that separates the proven franchise from the unproven programme - carries 30%.

Dispersion is enormous and honest: $231 bear to $1,003 bull. This is a high-conviction statement about which variable matters, not a high-conviction point estimate, and that variable is disclosed in late January 2027.
Rating AVOID: a price call, not a quality call. The disciplined entry is approximately $500, below which most outcomes are acceptable.
thesisImpact: Phase 5 contradicts nothing in Phases 1-4; it prices them. The franchise is exceptional and the programme is not yet earning. At $615.20 the market pays a full price for Family of Apps and marks the AI programme at roughly half of cost - defensible, and still leaving expected return below the cost of equity. The bear case has a date on it: FY2027 capex guidance in late January 2027.

memo.weighting: SOTP 30%, DCF 35%, EV/IC 25%, P/B-ROE 10%. The DCF is weighted below its default because roughly 87% of its value is terminal while the disputed variable is the shape of the next three years; the SOTP carries 30% because it is the only method that separates the extraordinary advertising franchise from the unproven capital programme, which is the entire question. Peer multiples are a cross-check only - the peer table could not be completed under this session's network policy. This is a price call, not a quality call: triangulated fair value $496 against $615.20, and an expected three-year IRR of 4.5% against a 10.0% cost of equity.

nonConsensus.market: Meta at 19.4x 2026 and 18.2x 2027 consensus EPS is the cheapest mega-cap AI asset.
nonConsensus.us: The consensus E is not reconcilable to the company's own guidance. On ~$252bn of revenue and guided expenses of $165-169bn, operating income is ~$85bn and EPS lands nearer $27 - about 14% below the $31.72 consensus - putting the real multiple at ~22.5x, not 19.4x.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 4: FY2026 total expense guidance of $165-169bn given with Q2 2026 results, against FY2025 operating income of $83.28bn and an FY2026E of ~$85bn on $51bn more revenue.

nonConsensus.market: The risk is that AI capex fails to pay off eventually; the advertising business itself is safe.
nonConsensus.us: The arithmetic is tighter and more immediate. At $12.8bn of required revenue per gigawatt, a $165bn capital year adds about $53bn to the annual revenue Meta must earn simply to cover its cost of capital - against actual annual revenue increments of $51-53bn. At the $180bn run-rate the 2027-28 plans imply, the hurdle grows about $58bn a year. The programme runs to stand still.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 2 unit cost curve (section 2.2) and Phase 3 section 3.2; incremental ROIC of 1.4% for 2025-26E and 6.4% for 2025-28E against a 9.5% WACC in Phase 4 section 4.4.

nonConsensus.market: The DMA and EU data regulation are the structural threat to Meta's targeting and pricing.
nonConsensus.us: Europe is Meta's fastest-pricing region at +19% per ad - the DMA has not bitten. The instrument that actually threatens the model is the August 2026 state AG settlement, whose design mandates (one-hour daily limits, nighttime blocks, age assurance) attack impressions, the term carrying 14 of the 27 points of growth, and which appears in no sell-side model.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 1 section 1.2 regional pricing table (Meta Q2 2026 results); the settlement terms reported 2026-08-26, including the 30% tranche contingent on YouTube and TikTok adopting equivalent measures.

fears.text: Committed cost sits behind a spot revenue book: roughly $279bn of not-yet-commenced lease obligations and a 5.5-year asset life, with no take-or-pay, no minimum volume and no indexation anywhere in the revenue.
fears.why: The precedent is exact and recent. In FY2022 revenue fell 1% and operating income fell 38%, from $46.75bn to $28.94bn. The committed 2027 cost base is roughly three times the 2022 base, and the leases cannot be cut.

fears.text: The compute has no second buyer. Meta open-weighted Muse Spark 1.2 and open-sourced Muse Glimmer, deliberately forgoing any model-licensing annuity.
fears.why: Every dollar of $137bn a year must be recovered through advertising and first-party products - in a year when OpenAI's ad run-rate went from about $100m to about $1bn in six months and TikTok's US joint venture became a fully funded, US-governed competitor. A regulated utility with stranded assets gets cost recovery; Meta gets a 5.5-year write-off.

fears.text: No one can stop it. Sixty-one percent of the votes sit with one holder who in 2026 alone raised capex guidance twice, suspended a $25bn buyback, funded the dividend with debt and reportedly considered an equity offering.
fears.why: There is no board mechanism, no proxy mechanism and no activist mechanism available to minority holders. If the programme doubles again, shareholders will read about it rather than vote on it.

sellTriggers: Incremental operating margin (delta operating income / delta revenue, y/y) below 10% for two consecutive quarters
Any primary equity issuance to fund the capital programme
Total debt/EBITDA above 1.5x for two consecutive quarters, or a downgrade below AA- / Aa3
Average price per ad growth below +5% y/y for two consecutive quarters
Family daily active people declining year-on-year in any quarter
